name: Learn latitude and longitude basics
blurb: How coordinates work, how to read and write them in the three common formats, and how to convert between them — useful for maps, emergencies and geocaching alike.
steps: Learn the system: latitude runs north and south from the equator, longitude east and west from Greenwich, both measured in degrees.
Learn the three formats — decimal degrees, degrees and decimal minutes, and degrees-minutes-seconds — and how to convert between them.
Learn the useful rule of thumb: one degree of latitude is about 111 km, and one minute is about one nautical mile, everywhere.
Learn why longitude distances shrink towards the poles.
Practise plotting given coordinates on a paper map and reading coordinates off it.
Learn to read out coordinates clearly for an emergency call, and know which format your local rescue services expect.
tips: Format confusion is the classic error — 40.5 degrees is not 40 degrees 5 minutes. Always state the format.
Getting the north/south or east/west designator wrong puts you on the wrong continent.
proof: You give your exact position in all three formats and plot a stranger’s coordinates on a paper map.
